motivation: EgoConseq-Bench evaluates whether a vision-language model can infer the visible local physical consequence of its own body executing a short action from one egocentric RGB image. The target is not navigation, object physics, or generic spatial relations; it is body-conditioned ego swept-volume consequence reasoning.

adjudication.rationale: Accept the phase-1 design with revisions: freeze the public design and executable case_generation_spec for pipeline verification, keep T1/T2/T4 core, keep T3/T5 as extensions, and mark all current cases as illustrative until simulator-backed artifacts exist.

design_principles: Single-image ego-action VQA: one RGB frame, one body description, one action primitive, one answer.
Body is a query-conditioned causal collision operator: do(body=r) can flip the consequence on the same image.
Distances are body-width normalized, with 1 body-width = 2r, avoiding absolute metric-distance claims from monocular RGB.
Labels come from deterministic swept-cylinder geometry and visibility filtering, not LLM judgment.
Core cases must be visible or directly inferable: no hidden-corner, off-image, or occluded decisive geometry.
Counterfactual body/action pairs, blind controls, option balancing, and shortcut heuristics are mandatory validity checks.
Swept-cylinder collision is the label engine, not the novelty claim; the novelty is the isolated diagnostic of MLLM embodied consequence grounding.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Forward swept-volume extent
inspired_by: EgoConseq swept-volume formula; VSI-Bench / Thinking in Space only as motivation-to-QA methodology inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Reads out how far the current body can move forward before first visible collision, normalized by body width.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible directional swept-volume comparison
inspired_by: EgoConseq action-conditioned visible collision evidence; prior spatial benchmarks only as coverage-design inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares which visible candidate sweep, or fixed visible horizon, remains collision-free for the queried body.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Short action-sequence consequence
inspired_by: MindCube only as what-if QA construction inspiration, not unseen-space reasoning
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Tests a small turn-then-forward consequence while retaining the visible-local swept-volume boundary.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-intervention consequence
inspired_by: Counterfactual QA methodology only; the intervention is EgoConseq's do(body=r) collision operator
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Holds image and action fixed while changing radius to test embodiment-sensitive consequence flips and no-flip controls.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward. How many body-widths can it move before first contact? Options: <2, 2-4, 4-8, >8.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute forward max_safe_distance_body_widths on the radius-specific navmesh and bin into <2 / 2-4 / 4-8 / >8; require bin_margin_body_widths >= 0.5.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Candidate directions: left-front {theta} degrees, straight, right-front {theta} degrees. Rank them by maximum distance before first contact, longest to shortest.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute swept distances for {-theta,0,+theta}, sort descending, and require visible evidence plus a ranking margin sufficient to avoid ties; theta defaults to 30 degrees with 15 degrees allowed.

tasks.question_template: Same RGB and action: move straight forward for {horizon} body-widths. Compare Body A radius {r_a} m and Body B radius {r_b} m, height 1.5 m. Which bodies complete the action without contact? Options use both / only smaller body / neither, unless body order is randomized.
tasks.answer_derivation: At the same pose/action/horizon, compare passability across radius-specific navmeshes; produce flip and no-flip controls with counterfactual_group_id and flip_pair_id.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Compare A) move straight forward and B) rotate {theta} degrees, then move forward. Which action allows more body-widths before first contact? Options: A, B, about the same.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compare straight max distance with turn-then-forward max distance; label about the same only within a fixed tie margin of 0.5 body-width. Extension-only until FOV support is verified.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move forward for {horizon} body-widths within the currently visible region. Is the swept body contact-free? Options: yes, no.
tasks.answer_derivation: Check whether every swept sample through the fixed horizon remains navigable for the radius-specific body. Extension-only until hidden-geometry and shortcut risks are audited.

qa_design.name: Body-Width Forward Horizon
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask how many body widths the queried cylindrical body can move straight forward before first visible contact.

qa_design.name: Visible Directional Sweep Ranking
qa_design.question_pattern: Rank left-front, straight, and right-front swept distances within the current FOV.

qa_design.name: Composite Motion Consequence
qa_design.question_pattern: Compare straight motion with a small turn-then-forward action under the same body constraints.

qa_design.name: Body Counterfactual Sweep
qa_design.question_pattern: Hold RGB and action fixed while changing body radius, then ask which bodies complete the sweep.

qa_design.name: Visible Passability
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask whether a fixed forward swept horizon in the visible region is contact-free for the queried body.

novelty_positioning: EgoConseq is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned consequence VQA; it is not route navigation, active exploration, or long-horizon planning.
The benchmark does not claim novel collision geometry; swept-cylinder intersection is the deterministic label engine.
Compared with PhysBench, it asks about the ego body rather than object or scene physics.
Compared with CapNav, it is one-step visible-local consequence reasoning rather than route-level capability-conditioned navigation.
Compared with TouchSafeBench, it uses a hypothetical action from single RGB rather than multi-view/current collision grounding.
Compared with ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench, it isolates body-width swept-volume collision/passability rather than broad affordance or scene-state evolution.
VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and ESI-Bench are cited only for benchmark-design discipline and adjacent positioning, not for importing their QA categories.

findings.claim: The strongest CVPR/ICLR diagnostic contribution is the isolation of ego-body action consequence reasoning from navigation, generic spatial relations, and object physics.
findings.evidence: goal.md defines the target as single RGB plus body description plus action primitive, labeled by body swept-volume intersection in the currently visible or directly inferable region.

findings.claim: T1, T2, and T4 should be the core demo tasks; T3 and T5 should remain extensions until visibility and ambiguity probes pass.
findings.evidence: T1 tests body-normalized metric extent, T2 tests visible configurational sweep comparison, and T4 directly tests the H3 body intervention; T3/T5 are labelable but more exposed to hidden-geometry and semantic-passability ambiguity.

findings.claim: The QA taxonomy should be derived from the EgoConseq label formula, not imported from VSI-Bench, MindCube, or ESI-Bench.
findings.evidence: VSI-Bench targets video spatial memory; MindCube targets limited-view mental models including unseen space; ESI-Bench targets active perception-action loops. They are useful as examples of motivation-to-QA discipline, while EgoConseq should derive QA types from body radius, action trajectory, visible swept volume, and collision evidence.

findings.claim: Near-neighbor contrast must include PhysBench, CapNav, TouchSafeBench, ENACT, EXPLORE-Bench, VSI-Bench, MindCube, and ESI-Bench.
findings.evidence: These cover object and scene physics, capability-conditioned route navigation, current or imminent collision grounding, egocentric interaction world modeling, long-horizon scene prediction, video spatial memory, limited-view spatial mental modeling, and active embodied spatial intelligence.

findings.claim: All five tasks are feasible in principle with a deterministic Habitat plus swept-cylinder pipeline, but only if every sample carries oracle and visibility metadata.
findings.evidence: goal.md already specifies radius-specific navmesh recomputation, depth projection for collision visibility, visible_sweep_ratio, hidden-geometry flags, bin margins, and counterfactual group IDs.

findings.claim: The current public state has no simulator-backed case manifest, so illustrative cases must not be treated as evaluation data.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null and blackboard coverage counts of zero for T1-T5.

findings.claim: The current phase permits illustrative case authoring rather than manifest-only selection.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has blackboard.phase=design and data_manifest_path=null.

findings.claim: Drafted 50 representative cases with 10 cases for each task T1-T5.
findings.evidence: Cases T1-01 through T5-10 cover metric measurement, configurational comparison, action mental simulation, embodied counterfactuals, and visible passability.

findings.claim: Questions avoid scene-specific answer leakage and keep geometric explanations outside the prompt text.
findings.evidence: Case questions specify body, action, candidates, and answer options; visibility assumptions and geometry are placed in visibility/rationale fields.

findings.claim: The benchmark is not yet publishable because there is no simulator-backed data manifest, oracle output, visibility audit, or baseline result.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null; blackboard coverage counts are 0 for T1-T5; case_generation_spec.status is bootstrap.

findings.claim: The core invalidity condition is hidden or visually underdetermined geometry.
findings.evidence: goal.md requires visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, collision_point_visible when applicable, requires_hidden_geometry=false, fov_supported=true, and bin_margin_body_widths >= 0.5 for T1.

findings.claim: The demo must empirically prove H1, H2, H3, human solvability, and oracle-label reliability; none can be assumed from the design text.
findings.evidence: goal.md defines validity as M4 near 95%+, blind M5 near random, best VLM well below oracle, and human/geometric annotators above VLM.

findings.claim: Showcase requirements are necessary but insufficient.
findings.evidence: The blackboard asks for 10 cases per task and text fields, but not mandatory rgb/depth/topdown/overlay paths, collision pixels, visibility ratios, bin margins, flip_pair_id, or heuristic-baseline outcomes in each reviewed case.

findings.claim: The drafted T4 template is currently unanswerable and leaks structure.
findings.evidence: T4-01 through T4-10 say 'specified horizon' but provide no numeric horizon; Body A is always smaller than Body B, making 'only B' structurally impossible under monotone collision geometry.

findings.claim: The illustrative cases can often be solved without ego-body swept-volume reasoning.
findings.evidence: T1 can reduce to center-ray depth or visible corridor length; T2/T3 to largest visible floor wedge; T4 to radius monotonicity and answer priors; T5 to radius/horizon priors unless counterfactual pairs and heuristics fail.

findings.claim: The case set nominally covers T1-T5, but executable design is over-narrowed to T1/T2/T4 until T3/T5 pass visibility filters.
findings.evidence: qa_design lists T1-T5, while case_generation_spec.tasks includes only T1, T2, and T4 as generated tasks.

findings.claim: Answer balance is incomplete, especially for T4.
findings.evidence: Case-author labels count T1 as 2/2/3/3 across bins, T3 as A/B/tie = 3/4/3, T5 as 5/5, but T4 has only A/both/neither = 4/3/3 and never 'only B'.

findings.claim: Novelty positioning remains vulnerable unless supported by citations and ablations against adjacent benchmarks.
findings.evidence: goal.md lists near neighbors, but the current manifest contains no bibliography, no formal task contrast table with cited protocols, and no evidence that generic spatial or collision heuristics fail.

findings.claim: Freeze T1, T2, and T4 as the core demo task families; keep T3 and T5 as extension families for the showcase and later validation.
findings.evidence: goal.md prioritizes T1/T2/T4 for the demo and marks T3/T5 as add-ons if visibility and ambiguity gates pass.

findings.claim: The final showcase may use VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and ESI-Bench only as methodology inspiration, not as copied QA taxonomies.
findings.evidence: The adjudicated taxonomy is derived from Body x Action_trajectory intersecting visible Scene_geometry: forward extent, directional sweep comparison, composite action consequence, body intervention, and fixed-horizon passability.

findings.claim: All 50 case_author cases are illustrative, not evaluation data.
findings.evidence: input_manifest.json has data_manifest_path=null, blackboard coverage counts are 0 for T1-T5, and the case visibility fields repeatedly use assumed visibility rather than oracle metadata.

findings.claim: The bootstrap case_generation_spec over-narrowed executable generation to T1/T2/T4; the adjudicated frozen spec preserves T3/T5 as extension generation targets so the benchmark is not reduced to three tasks.
findings.evidence: expert_reviewer flagged the mismatch between qa_design T1-T5 and case_generation_spec.tasks listing only T1/T2/T4.

findings.claim: No illustrative cases need removal, but T3 and T4 require revisions before HTML display as polished examples.
findings.evidence: T3 needs an explicit tie margin and FOV-supported post-turn visibility; T4 currently offers an impossible 'only B' distractor while Body A is always smaller.

findings.claim: Claims that must be marked not simulator-validated include all illustrative answers, all visibility assumptions, T1 bin occupancy, T2/T3 rankings, T4 flip/no-flip outcomes, T5 passability labels, and H1/H2/H3 validity-gate claims.
findings.evidence: No simulator-backed data_manifest, oracle trace, depth projection, baseline result, or human sanity result is available in this phase.

recommendations: Freeze the demo core as T1/T2/T4 with about 20 cases each, plus 10 cases each for T3/T5 as extension coverage, for an 80-case first demo.
Run survey mode before final sampling to verify T1 bin occupancy and adjust body-width bins only if the empirical distribution makes the draft bins unusable.
Use Fei-Fei Li spatial-intelligence benchmarks only as methodological references for benchmark discipline, not as sources of EgoConseq task categories.
State explicitly in the paper that swept-cylinder collision is the deterministic label engine, not the technical novelty.
Require case_author to include oracle, visibility, counterfactual, and display-asset fields so HTML cases can be audited before simulator validation.
Promote T3 or T5 to core only if the pipeline can produce enough unambiguous visible cases with balanced labels.
Report validity gates and shortcut baselines as part of the benchmark definition, not as optional experiments.
Use T1/T2/T4 as the demo core and treat T3/T5 as extension coverage until empirical visibility filters pass.
Run a template lint pass for banned leakage words before evaluation.
Keep these case IDs stable when simulator-backed manifest cases replace the illustrative answers.
Do not mark design_ready or showcase_ready until a real probe produces audited cases for T1/T2/T4 with oracle geometry, visibility metadata, and shortcut baselines.

Minimal continue gate: 60-100 demo cases, M4 at least 95%, M5 within about chance +5 percentage points, human at least best VLM +10 points, best M1 at least 15 points below M4, and nontrivial H3 pair-consistency failures by VLMs.
Stop or redesign if audited oracle labels disagree with rendered evidence on more than 5% of cases, if hidden-geometry filtering removes most candidates, or if humans cannot beat VLMs reliably.
Remove or downgrade any task where center-ray, floor-patch, corridor-width, radius-only, action-only, or answer-prior baselines approach model performance.

For every public showcase case, require rgb_path, depth_path, topdown_path, sweep_overlay_path, max_safe_distance_body_widths, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, bin_margin_body_widths, flip_pair_id, and heuristic predictions.

Fix T4 before use: specify the action horizon, randomize small/large body labels, add flip_pair_id/counterfactual_group_id, and avoid an answer option that is mathematically impossible under radius monotonicity.
Keep T3/T5 as extension evidence only; do not claim full action mental simulation or passability coverage until their real cases pass the same visibility and shortcut gates as T1/T2/T4.
Add a formal removal gate for template leakage: any prompt whose text alone lets M5 exceed chance materially should be rewritten or removed.
Set the next phase to pipeline_verify. Do not spend another round debating the design unless the probe fails a gate.
Produce `case_generation_spec.frozen.json` from the design_doc below as the exact handoff artifact for pipeline_verify.
Produce `ego_conseq_showcase_illustrative.html`: goal + task taxonomy + 10 illustrative cases per T1-T5, with every case marked not simulator-validated.
Produce `ego_conseq_design_rationale.html`: motivation, design principles, near-neighbor positioning, validity gates, baselines, and why prior spatial benchmarks are inspiration only.
Pipeline_verify should next output `pipeline_probe_manifest.json` with at least T1/T2/T4 audited cases containing rgb/depth/topdown/overlay paths and oracle/visibility metadata.
After simulator-backed cases exist, replace or relabel illustrative answers rather than treating them as ground truth.

risks.risk: Reviewers may dismiss the benchmark as only wall-collision detection.
risks.mitigation: Frame the task family as metric consequence, configurational comparison, short action simulation, and embodied counterfactual reasoning; report T1/T2/T4 separately and use T3/T5 only after validation.

risks.risk: Single-image monocular scale ambiguity could make some labels visually underdetermined.
risks.mitigation: Use body-width normalization, discard bin-boundary cases, require visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, require collision visibility where relevant, and run human sanity checks.

risks.risk: Hidden geometry could turn the benchmark into guessing around corners or behind occluders.
risks.mitigation: Core cases must have requires_hidden_geometry=false, fov_supported=true, ambiguous=false, and visible decisive evidence.

risks.risk: Language priors, radius priors, answer imbalance, or action priors could explain model performance.
risks.mitigation: Use same-image counterfactual groups, balanced labels, blind M5, radius-only/action-only baselines, majority baselines, and geometric heuristics such as center-ray and corridor-width controls.

risks.risk: Habitat navmesh labels may not match what is visually legible from RGB.
risks.mitigation: Store RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, collision pixel, geometric explanation, and visible evidence notes; manually audit showcase cases before scaling.

risks.risk: T4 flip cases may be sparse or too subtle in random samples.
risks.mitigation: Run a survey pass over scenes and radii first, then stratified rejection sample around visible bottlenecks while retaining no-flip controls.

risks.risk: Prompt wording may leak labels through spatial adjectives.
risks.mitigation: Lint templates against banned answer-revealing words and keep scene explanations in display-only fields.

risks.risk: If oracle, blind, human, and VLM validity gates do not separate cleanly, the paper claim collapses.
risks.mitigation: Treat the demo as a go/no-go probe: stop or redesign if M4 is not high, M5 is not near random, humans do not beat VLMs, or VLMs approach the oracle.

risks.risk: These are illustrative cases, not simulator-oracle labels.
risks.mitigation: Replace or verify every answer with Habitat swept-cylinder labels once data_manifest.json is available.

risks.risk: T3 and T5 are more vulnerable to hidden-geometry ambiguity than T1/T2/T4.
risks.mitigation: Only keep T3/T5 cases with fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, and requires_hidden_geometry=false.

risks.risk: Some display cases require an indicated local target or direction overlay in the rendered prompt package.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the final HTML/data view includes the target/action marker when the question references an indicated target.

risks.risk: Published benchmark collapses into visible corridor-width or wall-distance classification rather than body-conditioned swept-volume reasoning.
risks.mitigation: Require center-ray, largest-floor-patch, corridor-width, radius-only, action-only, and majority baselines to stay near chance or clearly below M1/humans.

risks.risk: Labels disagree with what a single RGB image supports because navmesh collision points are outside view, behind occluders, or created by depth/rendering artifacts.
risks.mitigation: Gate every case with saved RGB/depth/topdown/sweep overlay, collision_point_pixel, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and manual audit.

risks.risk: T4 becomes a monotonic-radius quiz instead of an embodied counterfactual test.
risks.mitigation: Randomize body A/B order, remove impossible distractors or score against a monotonic prior baseline, specify horizon, and require same-image flip plus no-flip groups.

risks.risk: Single-image monocular scale makes T1 bins visually noisy near thresholds.
risks.mitigation: Freeze bins only after survey histograms; discard bin_margin_body_widths < 0.5; report human agreement and ordinal off-by-one error.

risks.risk: Prompt/template leakage makes M5 non-random.
risks.mitigation: Lint prompts for banned geometry words, balance templates, and fail or revise any task where blind M5 exceeds chance by more than a small tolerance.

risks.risk: T3 and long-horizon T5 require predicting around turns, outside the FOV, or beyond reliable visible evidence.
risks.mitigation: Keep T3/T5 extension-only until fov_supported and visible_sweep_ratio pass on real cases; remove any sample with decisive hidden geometry.

risks.risk: Taxonomy may look borrowed from spatial-intelligence benchmarks rather than derived from EgoConseq's formula.
risks.mitigation: Name categories directly from swept-volume readouts and cite external taxonomies only as methodological inspiration, not as task definitions.

risks.risk: Live pipeline verification is blocked if the Habitat environment, HM3D/MP3D paths, radius-specific navmesh recomputation, or writeable artifact directory are unavailable under --runner codex.
risks.mitigation: Start pipeline_verify with a small environment probe that saves RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, and data_manifest entries before generating the full demo.

risks.risk: Oracle labels may be wrong if navmesh erosion is double-counted or visibility projection is mishandled.
risks.mitigation: Recompute navmesh per radius, use 0.05m stepping, store collision pixels, and manually audit at least 20 probe cases.

risks.risk: Illustrative HTML may be mistaken for validated benchmark evidence.
risks.mitigation: Add a visible 'illustrative only / not simulator-validated' badge to every non-oracle case and keep empirical claims out of the HTML until pipeline_verify passes.

risks.risk: Prompt wording, answer priors, radius-only priors, or center-ray heuristics can create shortcut solutions.
risks.mitigation: Run prompt lint, balance answer distributions, and report M5, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, and corridor-width baselines.

risks.risk: T3 and T5 can drift into hidden-space inference rather than visible local consequence reasoning.
risks.mitigation: Keep them extension-only until visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, fov_supported=true, collision evidence visibility, and requires_hidden_geometry=false are verified.

risks.risk: Current T4 wording creates a monotonicity shortcut because 'only B' is impossible when Body B is always larger.
risks.mitigation: Either remove 'only B' from the answer space or randomize body order and label choices as only smaller / only larger with explicit radius metadata.
